newsitem.title: CHINA: China crude oil industry seen losses in 1997.
newsitem.headline: China crude oil industry seen losses in 1997.

text.p: China's crude oil industry could be in the red in 1997, the Economic Information Daily quoted a forecast by the China National Petroleum Corp as saying on Tuesday.
However, company officials reached by telephone declined to comment.
The newspaper attributed the losses to the rising costs of exploitation coupled with shrinking output at China's eastern and northern onshore fields.

The Daqing oilfield in northeastern Heilongjiang province has seen costs of exploiting its oil increase each year by about 3.0 billion yuan ($360 million) in order to maintain stable output, it said, but gave no further details.
China's crude oil production in 1997 was expected to be 152.5 million tonnes, while production in 1996 was 158.51 million tonnes, up 6.37 percent from 1995.
